ACCEPT. The averaging identity is exact, and it fully proves the stated source-only coefficient-one theorem without any restriction on  $X$  or  $K$ , under the retained normalization, ownership, strip, and receiver hypotheses.The decisive point is that every physical no- $P$  deficit occurs in at most two strip sums. In the source-only case,
$$2D_G\ \ge\ \sum_iD_i\ \ge\ 2B,$$
so the physical union supplies enough deficit to pay the  $B$  whole source charges.1. The exact averaging identity is correctWrite
$$S'=\sum_iD'_i\ge0.$$
Summing the accepted strip identities gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\sum_iD_i
&=2C+\sum_iL_i+\sum_i(U_i-S_i)+A+S'\\
&=2C+(2B-2C)+F+A+S'\\
&=2B+F+A+S'.
\end{aligned}$$
By the stated coverage multiplicities,
$$\sum_iD_i=D_1+2D_2,
\qquad
D_G=D_1+D_2.$$
Consequently,
$$2D_G=\sum_iD_i+D_1.$$
Substituting into the original whole-receiver ledger,
$$\Delta=-B+D_G+R,$$
yields
$$\begin{aligned}
2\Delta
&=-2B+2D_G+2R\\
&=-2B+\sum_iD_i+D_1+2R\\
&=\boxed{F+A+S'+D_1+2R}.
\end{aligned}$$
Every term on the right other than  $F$  is nonnegative. Therefore
$$F\ge0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\Delta\ge0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
|T_0|+|M_0|\le\frac{mn}{2}.$$
There is no omitted crossing term. Doubly covered no- $P$  tiles are accounted for exactly by the coefficient two in  $\sum_iD_i$ . The number of such tiles never needs a bound.2. Source-only coverage does imply  $F=0$ Coalescing overlapping or adjacent mouth intervals in a physical band produces exactly their union of physical tiles. It introduces no additional tiles between separated mouths.Thus every endpoint in a coalesced strip already lies in an original mouth. Under the source-only assumption and the retained preservation of mouth labels, every such endpoint belongs to a prescribed source.It follows that no complete-comb endpoint lies in a strip. In particular, no physical sparse or saturated singleton end tile of a complete comb belongs to any strip: such a tile would contain a comb endpoint in the strip.Hence every comb-end strip multiplicity is zero, and
$$F=0.$$
The exact identity becomes
$$\boxed{\Delta=\frac{A+S'+D_1}{2}+R\ge0.}$$
This proves the claimed theorem for any finite feasible configuration of the prescribed positive long sources, with all allowed tile-preserving orientations, source contacts, and mouth intersections, subject to the unchanged outside-coverage and receiver hypotheses.Combs outside the mouths are allowed.For precision, I would phrase “no complete comb meets a strip” as “no complete-comb endpoint meets a strip.” Selected supports belonging to a comb outside the mouths might enter a strip. Such selections are already included in the actual  $t_Q$  counts and do not create comb-end multiplicities. This wording distinction does not affect the proof.3. No receiver charge or actual matching contribution is reusedThe resource interpretation is valid because it operates solely on physical no- $P$  deficits.If a physical donor tile  $Q$  belongs to  $m_Q\in\{1,2\}$  strips, assigning half of its deficit to each incident strip uses
$$\frac{m_Qd_Q}{2}\le d_Q.$$
Specifically:A singly covered tile supplies  $d_Q/2$ , leaving  $d_Q/2$  unused.A doubly covered tile supplies two halves, totaling exactly  $d_Q$ .Thus the total assigned amount is
$$\frac12\sum_iD_i
=
B+\frac{F+A+S'}2,$$
and the unused amount inside  $G$  is exactly
$$D_G-\frac12\sum_iD_i=\frac{D_1}{2}.$$
When  $F\ge0$ , these assignments cover the total source charge  $B$ .The whole source charges enter once, through the term  $-B$  in the original receiver ledger. Complete combs retain their zero whole charge, and the remaining receiver deficits enter once through  $R$ . No source charge is separately charged to both strip directions.Likewise, no actual matching edge or corrected matching transfer is allocated again. The half weights are numerical bookkeeping on physical no- $P$  deficits. All matching contributions remain in the accepted whole-component ledger.The auxiliary quantities  $A$  and  $D'_i$  establish the strip inequalities; they are not additional physical donor collections. Indeed, in the source-only case the proof can simply discard them:
$$D_G\ge\frac12\sum_iD_i
=\frac12(2B+A+S')
\ge B.$$
4. The more general comb condition is sufficientFor each complete comb  $C$ , let
$$m_s(C),m_u(C)\in\{0,1,2\}$$
be the strip multiplicities of its sparse and saturated singleton end tiles, with a missing end assigned multiplicity zero. Then
$$F=\sum_C\bigl(m_u(C)-m_s(C)\bigr).$$
Therefore the termwise condition
$$m_u(C)\ge m_s(C)\qquad\text{for every complete comb }C$$
implies  $F\ge0$ , and hence coefficient one.Your distinction from union closure is correct. Union membership records only whether a multiplicity is positive. It does not distinguish, for example,
$$m_s=2,\qquad m_u=1,$$
whose contribution to  $F$  would be  $-1$ , even though both ends belong to  $G$ . No sufficiency of  $O=0$  follows from those flags alone.5. The deduction is consistent with the crossing-loss identityLet  $u_\times,s_\times$  count saturated and sparse comb-end crossing tiles. The earlier definitions give
$$F=J-O+u_\times-s_\times,$$
and, since  $D_2$  is exactly the deficit on no- $P$  crossing tiles,
$$K=D_2+s_\times-u_\times.$$
Therefore
$$F=J-O+D_2-K.$$
These relations reconcile the averaging identity with the previously accepted exact crossing ledger. The stronger source-only conclusion comes from using the multiplicity bound and its nonnegative slack.In particular, for source-only mouth coverage,
$$J=O=u_\times=s_\times=0,\qquad K=D_2,$$
and
$$D_1+2K=2B+A+S'.$$
Thus the earlier expression for the available margin satisfies
$$B-K+A+S'
=
\frac{A+S'+D_1}{2}\ge0.$$
This explicitly shows why an independent condition  $K\le B$  is unnecessary: the quantities in the exact ledger already enforce the required compensation.The crossing-loss and averaging estimates are two bounds derived from the same ledger. One may use whichever is stronger; their supplies cannot be added.No mathematical revision is needed. The deduction removes the  $X/K$  restriction for the stated class of prescribed sources with source-only mouth endpoint coverage. Coverage of arbitrary positive bent components remains a separate question.
